rule: Each value: dB by which a measure would raise sound B to make it as loud as sound A, or the level difference the row's question names. 'agrees': within 1 dB of the published range (or the right sign, at least 0.5 dB); 'near': within 3 dB; 'off': further; 'no effect': under 0.5 dB where a sign is expected; 'opposite': the wrong sign.
caution: Each row says what was read of its paper and what was assumed. The published ranges come from small panels, and for the largest temporal integration later studies of the same laboratory found more. This constrains a model. It does not validate one for sound effects.

literatureModel.note: literature.L0 was set from the rows in 'fitted'; only the rows in 'heldOut' test it; those in 'addedAfterFitting' entered the benchmark after the model was fitted and were never fitted; 'notModelled' it is expected to fail

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, 1 kHz tone, where it is largest
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms tone lies above the equally loud 200 ms tone, the 5 ms tone held at 56 dB SPL
phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996), JASA 99(3):1633-1644; 6 listeners, adaptive two-interval matching: a peak of 18 to 19 dB when the 5 ms tone is about 56 dB SPL
phenomena.stimulusFrom: abstract (journal and 1995 meeting); the tones' gating from Buus, Florentine & Poulsen (1999), which says the 1996 study used the same; the paper itself is behind a paywall and was not read
phenomena.reconstruction: later studies of the same laboratory with a roving-level procedure found maxima of 26 to 27 dB (Buus et al. 1999)

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, 1 kHz tone, high level
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms tone lies above the equally loud 200 ms tone, the 5 ms tone held at 100 dB SPL
phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996), JASA 99(3):1633-1644; 6 listeners, adaptive two-interval matching: about 10 dB near 100 dB SPL
phenomena.stimulusFrom: abstract (journal and 1995 meeting); the tones' gating from Buus, Florentine & Poulsen (1999), which says the 1996 study used the same; the paper itself is behind a paywall and was not read
phenomena.reconstruction: 'about 10 dB' taken as 9 to 11; 'near 100 dB SPL' taken as the 5 ms tone's level (Buus et al. 1999 give 11 dB with the 200 ms tone at 90)

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, broadband noise, where it is largest
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms noise lies above the equally loud 200 ms noise, the 5 ms noise held at 76 dB SPL
phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996), JASA 99(3):1633-1644; 6 listeners, adaptive two-interval matching: a peak of 18 to 19 dB when the 5 ms noise is about 76 dB SPL
phenomena.stimulusFrom: abstract (journal and 1995 meeting); the tones' gating from Buus, Florentine & Poulsen (1999), which says the 1996 study used the same; the paper itself is behind a paywall and was not read
phenomena.reconstruction: noise 20 Hz to 20 kHz, gated like the tones: the noise's bandwidth and gating were not available

phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996), JASA 99(3):1633-1644; 6 listeners, adaptive two-interval matching: about 13 dB near 100 dB SPL
phenomena.stimulusFrom: abstract (journal and 1995 meeting); the tones' gating from Buus, Florentine & Poulsen (1999), which says the 1996 study used the same; the paper itself is behind a paywall and was not read

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, 1 kHz tone, 30 against 200 ms
phenomena.question: dB the 30 ms tone must be raised to match the 200 ms tone
phenomena.source: Buus, Florentine & Poulsen (1997), JASA 101(2):669-680, on the 1996 data: a maximum of about 7 dB
phenomena.stimulusFrom: Buus et al. (1997), read in the paper, for the number; gating as in the rows above
phenomena.reconstruction: the 200 ms tone at 37.5 dB SPL, its level when as loud as the 5 ms tone at 56 dB SPL; the paper gives no level for this maximum

phenomena.title: A rising tone is louder than the same tone falling
phenomena.question: dB the falling tone must be raised to match the rising one
phenomena.source: Ponsot, Susini & Meunier (2015), Atten. Percept. Psychophys. 77(3):907-920: 3.4 and 3.2 dB by matching (10 and 12 listeners), 5.3 and 3.1 dB by magnitude estimation (16 each)
phenomena.reconstruction: 1 kHz, 2 s, 60 to 75 dB SPL linear in dB, 10 ms gating: one of the paper's seven ranges; the asymmetry was smaller for the ramps reaching 80 to 90 dB SPL

phenomena.title: An impact-like envelope is softer than its time reverse (tone)
phenomena.question: dB the slow-attack, fast-decay sound must be lowered to match the impact-like one
phenomena.source: Stecker & Hafter (2000), JASA 107(6):3358-3368: 1 to 3 dB for one listener after impact-like standards, under 1 dB after the others; the same sign by magnitude estimation for tones and noise (8 listeners each) and from 330 Hz to 6 kHz
phenomena.evidence: single study; the sign is the finding, the size is weak
phenomena.reconstruction: 250 ms, the paper's envelope family with sharpness 3 and peak-time parameter 3, 330 Hz tone, peak equal to a sinusoid's at 80 dB SPL; one line of the envelope's equation was unreadable in the copy and was completed from the properties the paper states

phenomena.title: An impact-like envelope is softer than its time reverse (noise)

phenomena.evidence: single study; the sign is the finding, the size is weak
phenomena.reconstruction: 250 ms, the paper's envelope family with sharpness 3 and peak-time parameter 3, white noise, peak equal to a sinusoid's at 80 dB SPL; one line of the envelope's equation was unreadable in the copy and was completed from the properties the paper states

phenomena.title: A slow train of impulses is as loud as one impulse
phenomena.question: dB the train must be raised to match the single impulse (none)
phenomena.source: Ogura, Suzuki & Sone (1991), J. Acoust. Soc. Jpn (E) 12(1):1-11: no change up to 0.2-0.7 impulses a second
phenomena.stimulusFrom: abstract only: the paper's file could not be fetched (the journal's site refuses automated reading)
phenomena.reconstruction: noise impulse of 50 ms, three of them 4 s apart (0.25 a second); 'as loud' taken as within 1 dB

phenomena.title: A fast train of impulses is louder than one impulse
phenomena.question: dB the train must be lowered to match the single impulse
phenomena.source: Ogura, Suzuki & Sone (1991): above the critical rate loudness grows with rate
phenomena.stimulusFrom: abstract only: the paper's file could not be fetched (the journal's site refuses automated reading)
phenomena.reconstruction: the same impulse, ten of them 0.2 s apart (5 a second)

phenomena.title: A 63 Hz octave band of noise against a 1 kHz band
phenomena.question: dB the 63 Hz band must be raised to match the 1 kHz band
phenomena.source: Fenton & Lee (2017), AES 143rd Convention: 13 listeners, method of adjustment, one loudspeaker at 2 m, the 1 kHz band at 75 dB; listeners gave about 9.98 dB at 63 Hz
phenomena.reconstruction: octave bands of pink noise through 8th-order filters, both at 75 dB SPL, 2 s (the paper looped them); 9.98 dB taken as 9 to 11

phenomena.title: A 125 Hz octave band of noise against a 1 kHz band
phenomena.question: dB the 125 Hz band must be raised to match the 1 kHz band
phenomena.source: Fenton & Lee (2017), AES 143rd Convention: 13 listeners, method of adjustment, one loudspeaker at 2 m, the 1 kHz band at 75 dB; Table 1 gives BS.1770's error for this band (-3.79 dB)
phenomena.evidence: single study; the value is derived
phenomena.reconstruction: the listeners' gain is derived: BS.1770's gain as computed here (+1.63 dB) minus the paper's error; the paper's own BS.1770 value is printed for 63 Hz only and is 0.8 dB under this project's, so 1.5 dB either side is allowed

phenomena.title: A louder beginning counts for more than a louder middle
phenomena.question: dB the sound with the louder middle must be raised to match the one with the louder beginning
phenomena.source: Fischenich, Hots, Verhey, Guldan & Oberfeld (2021), PLoS ONE 16(12):e0261001: for contiguous 100 ms segments the first weighs 4 to 5 times a later one, falling off over 200 to 300 ms; no primacy when the segments are 500 ms apart. Pedersen & Ellermeier (2008), JASA 123(2):963-972: the same without feedback, and flat weights for listeners given feedback
phenomena.reconstruction: 1 s white noise in ten 100 ms segments at 55 dB SPL, 5 dB more in the first or in the sixth; the papers measured weights from random level changes of 2 to 2.5 dB, not this contrast; with their weights it would be worth about 1 dB
